bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR on Askbot avatar mutation views. `admin_or_owner_required` in askbot/views/avatar_views.py is supposed to allow only an administrator or the profile owner, but two interacting mistakes let any authenticated user change another user's avatar: (1) it compared `request.user.id` (int) to the Django URL capture `user_id` (always a string from `^avatar/upload/(?P<user_id>\d+)/$` and sibling routes), so the owner check never succeeded in Python 2 or 3; (2) when that check failed it fell through to `login_required(func)(request, user_id)`, which only tests authentication and then still invokes the view. The decorated sinks (`upload`, `set_primary`, `enable_gravatar`, `enable_default_avatar`, `disable_gravatar`) then `get_object_or_404(User, pk=user_id)` and write the victim's Avatar/avatar_type. A logged-in attacker POSTs to `/avatar/upload/<victim_id>/` (or intercepts and rewrites user_id) and replaces the victim's profile picture. CVE-2026-1213 remains PUBLISHED (Fluid Attacks CNA; GHSA withdrawn_at=null).
flaw_origin: The IDOR was born in 929cba67ae17fc5183001adf4f732e30c0b635da (2015-03-16, Evgeny Fadeev), which replaced the old `@login_required` add/change views that always mutated `request.user` with new user_id-parameterized avatar views and the first `admin_or_owner_required` decorator (`request.user.id == user_id` plus login_required fallthrough). Parent 7815540b2f2266a710e5063b8bad1c222d9b930b has no `admin_or_owner_required` and no `user.id == user_id` comparison. Later bf1404763df59f203e5da99ff5c48cd7f46458ef only changed `is_authenticated()` to the Django 2 property; it did not rewrite the comparison or the deny path.

reasoning: CVE-2026-1213/GHSA-r2jv-fwfr-4j8c is a real published CWE-639, not withdrawn: any authenticated Askbot user can overwrite another user's profile picture by supplying that user's id to avatar mutation endpoints. The sink is `admin_or_owner_required` failing to deny non-owners because an int/str equality never matches a Django URL capture and the else-path still runs the view via login_required. Line-history and pickaxe both identify 929cba67ae17fc5183001adf4f732e30c0b635da as the smallest first-write of that decorator and of the user_id-parameterized upload/set_primary/enable_* views; the immediate parent still uses request.user-only @login_required add/change helpers, so the IDOR surface and the broken check appear together in one ordinary single-parent feature commit (not a move, revert, backport, or squash aggregate). bf140476 only modernized is_authenticated and is not the BIC. The first public patch of the mechanism is 3da3d75f35204aa71633c7a315327ba39cb6295d (int() coerce + 403), which the advisory and the 0.12.3 changelog cite; no finer public member reconstructs from the single-parent release object. The BIC is an ancestor of both v0.12.2 and the fix. AI attribution is taken only from that 2015 commit object: author and committer are Evgeny Fadeev, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot identity, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
